# Psalm 63 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.

**2** O God, You are my God; earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You; my flesh faints for You, as in a dry and weary land where there is no water.

**3** So I have looked upon You in the sanctuary, beholding Your power and glory.

**4** Because Your steadfast love is better than life, my lips will praise You.

**5** So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift up my hands.

**6** My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise You with joyful lips,

**7** when I remember You upon my bed, and meditate on You in the watches of the night;

**8** for You have been my help, and in the shadow of Your wings I will sing for joy.

**9** My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me.

**10** But those who seek to destroy my life shall go down into the depths of the earth;

**11** they shall be given over to the power of the sword; they shall be a portion for jackals.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 63.

- **63:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **63:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **63:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **63:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **63:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **63:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **63:4**: 'Your steadfast love is better than life' — the single most radical value claim in the Psalter. God's love outweighs existence itself.

### LOGOS
- **63:9**: 'My soul clings to You' — the verb davaq (cling/cleave) is the same used in Genesis 2:24 for the marriage bond. This is covenant intimacy.

### PNEUMA
- **63:1-2**: The wilderness setting makes the thirst metaphor literal. David is physically parched in the Judean desert — and his spiritual thirst mirrors his physical need.

— SOPHIA
